Use case: style-transfer. Create a new chapter-specific derivative of reference image 1 as a finished production environment for a children's English-learning journey map. Preserve the approved illustration's soft painterly volume, warm cream stone, muted coral/terracotta, teal accents, rounded edges, upper-left sunshine and gentle contact shadows. Reference image 2 is additional style/material guidance only. Replace the architecture and layout as specified below; do not copy either earlier chapter's geography.
Canvas: EXACT tall 1:3 native aspect ratio, preferably 724x2172 (height exactly three times width), opaque RGB. One geographically coherent uninterrupted scene, not three stacked illustrations. Parallel oblique/isometric projection with one consistent camera, human-scale doors and masonry; no horizon restart. The central floor must connect continuously from top to bottom at one ground level.
The runtime places three existing character groups in contiguous square sections; do NOT generate those characters. Their visible height is 36% of one square. Doors should be large enough for these storybook adults, not miniature dollhouse portals.
Keep flat, uncluttered cream paving in global rectangles x=23%-77%, y=14%-23%, y=47%-56%, y=80%-89%. The feet centers are (50%,18.67%), (50%,52%), (50%,85.33%). All the width around these contact zones must be true level floor, not steps, grass, rugs, drains, furniture or threshold edges. Keep x=30%-70% visually quiet just below each feet center for separate stars and Lesson buttons. This must look like natural usable floor, not blank circular UI platforms.
All roofs, pillars, tree trunks, raised planters, benches, walls and furnishings stay at the outside edges of the standing zones. The same floor continues between them, with no horizontal seam, cliff, transverse wall, raised dais or unconnected path.
No people, animals, floating platforms, water canals, S bridges, repeated circular terraces, letters, numbers, logos, writing, signs, UI, stars, medals, pins or watermarks. No teaching props (clothing on hangers, passports, luggage, books held out, ice cream cones, glasses or cups); the unchanged character art already contains the only lesson props.
CHAPTER IDENTITY: a welcoming covered VISITORS' GALLERY, clearly different from a residential street and a waterside garden. A broad, gently bending tiled arcade connects a home foyer, an arrivals reception and an office entrance. Cream square columns and partial terracotta roof eaves form a rhythm mainly along the LEFT edge; teal-framed tall doors/windows and small inset wall alcoves are at the side edges. The RIGHT edge is mostly open to a quiet planted courtyard with a low cream balustrade, not another row of street houses. Keep the main walkway open to the viewer.
Upper third: a domestic foyer with a teal door, soft plain curtains and an empty decorative wall niche, suggesting a friendly home visit. No clothing shop.
Middle third: a more formal visitors' reception portico with wide teal-framed glazing and a small EMPTY wooden check-in counter recessed to the far side; nothing extends into the central foot zone. No airplanes, flags, official symbols or written signs.
Lower third: a modest open office entry with broad rectangular windows, a side potted plant and a glimpse of an EMPTY side desk inside. No school, classroom or children.
These three uses appear ALONG ONE continuous same-level gallery, never three rooms pasted vertically. Vary the architecture as one walks along, while preserving the same tile scale and sunlight. Use restrained foliage at the sides, mostly architectural rhythm and generous paved floor. Finished warm and inviting game environment, compatible with the previously approved character silhouettes.
